item.title: How Did Nashville Become Music’s Hottest Hub? | Billboard On The Record
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to Billboard On The Record, I'm your host Kristin Robinson. Today, we're talking about the rise of country music and how it's taken over the charts. Joining me is Seth England, CEO of Big Loud, the label behind artists like Morgan Wallen, Florida Georgia Line, and HARDY. Seth, thanks for being here.
Seth England: Thank you for having me.
Host: Country music has become a huge force in the industry, with Nashville no longer just a country town. Seth, can you tell us about how Big Loud has helped shape the modern country landscape?
Seth England: I don't think this country bubble has burst. The fans are now driving what's popular, and we're seeing a lot of exciting new talent emerge.
Host: That's interesting. How do you think country radio has evolved? Is it still about breaking new songs, or has it become more like pop, where it's the end destination?
Seth England: The gatekeepers used to choose what was popular, but now the fans are telling us what to playlist. We're seeing a shift in how songs are discovered and promoted.
Host: What about Nashville? How do you think the city will change as pop moves on to other genres?
Seth England: Nashville has become a hub for songwriters across genres. We're seeing a lot of collaboration and crossover, which is exciting for the music industry as a whole.
Host: That's really interesting. And finally, what drives hit-making today, and how does Big Loud approach artist development?
Seth England: Artist development is one of our most important pillars. We focus on finding and nurturing new talent, and giving them the support they need to succeed.
[Outro music plays]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to this episode of Billboard On The Record. Don't forget to rate, review, and subscribe so you never miss an episode. You can also follow us on Instagram, TikTok, Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and YouTube @billboard. Thanks to Seth England for joining us today, and we'll catch you on the next episode.
